title: midweek-inference-grok-action-log-nov10-2026
content:
Midweek inference grok & action log — 2026-11-10

Attendees: Sofia Patel (notes/owner), Marcus Chen, Priya Rao, Daniel Ortega, Aisha Mohammed, on-call: Jenny K.
Duration: 40m standup-style sync, followed by 20m deep-dive
Meeting purpose: quick status updates + align on rolling experiments (kernel micro-optimizations, KV-cache eviction tuning, batching heuristics) and surface blockers for SRE/infra.

High-level takeaways
- Kernel micro-patch (PR #1145) reduced 2x-latency tail for short-context requests in our sanity bench but has a memory regression on p4d-8s at high concurrency. We will gate by instance type for now. (Owner: Marcus)
- KV-cache eviction policy test (LFU vs TTL-hybrid) showing 7–12% token-cost reduction on warm-dialog workloads; some regression on single-turn chat where prefix reuse is low. (Owner: Priya)
- Adaptive batching experiment (heuristic B2) improved throughput by 18% but added 6–12ms median latency for interactive traffic. Deciding trade-off for Dedicated pools. (Owner: Daniel)

Notes / discussion
1) Kernel micro-optimizations
- Marcus summarized bench results: local synthetic suite shows median token latency unchanged, p95 improved ~9–13% for seq_len < 64. Tail (p99) improved ~2x in controlled tests.
- Issue: memory footprint increase ~5–10% on large-batch runs on p4d-8s. Hypothesis: added optimizer buffer in the new attention kernel is not reusing a pooled allocator path.
- Action: Marcus to add allocator fallback and re-run stress test on p4d-8s by 2026-11-12. If fallback reduces tail benefits <10% then we will only enable patch for rtx-6000 fleets.
- Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/1145 (bench logs in PR comments).

2) KV-cache eviction policy experiments
- Priya walked through the LFU vs TTL-hybrid test on two workloads: customer-A (multi-turn support chat) and customer-B (sessionless summarization).
- Findings: LFU wins on multi-turn (cache hit rate +12%, token compute cost -8%); TTL-hybrid wins on sessionless (less aggressive stale retention -> -3% tail latency).
- Open question: how to route mixed workloads within the same Dedicated pool.
- Decision: implement a per-route policy flag allowing customer to pick eviction profile; default remains TTL-hybrid for hosted API. Priya to prototype config UI for console (mock) and push config API by 2026-11-19.
- Metrics dashboards to add: per-route KV hit-rate, eviction churn, and per-token cost delta. Owner: Observability (Aisha + console team).

3) Adaptive batching heuristic B2
- Daniel presented B2: prefer batching up to a soft latency budget (x ms) then flush; uses prediction model for short vs long completion. On eval set, throughput +18% w.r.t current B1, but median latency added 6–12ms on interactive routes.
- Discussion: For Dedicated customers with firm SLAs, we can toggle B2 per deployment class. For hosted, B2 maybe acceptable behind a premium flag.
- Action: Daniel to add ab-test route config and run a 48h canary on a small subset (5% traffic) starting 2026-11-12. Rollback criteria: median latency increase >10ms on customer visible routes or p95 increase >5%.

4) Observability gaps surfaced
- We still lack fine-grained traces tying a specific kernel version to end-to-end percentiles. Aisha proposes adding kernel-version tagging in traces and surface on per-route latency heatmaps.
- Action: Aisha to file infra ticket and deliver a patch to tracing agent by 2026-11-15. Add a dashboard panel that compares last 4 kernel builds for p50/p95/p99.

5) Blockers / operational items
- On-call reported intermittent OOMs on rtx-6000 pools when enabling new kernel; suspected allocation leak. Blocking wider rollout. (Ops owner: Jenny K.)
- Action: Jenny to collect heap dump and allocation profile during a repro window (2026-11-11 02:00 PST). Marcus to be on-call for analysis.

6) Customer-impact check
- No major incidents reported. A small customer (internal staging for Customer-X) saw higher latencies during B2 pilot last week — they are on Dedicated. Solutions: per-customer batching flags + canary rollouts. Sales/SE notified to coordinate with Customer-X.

7) Small experiments / quick wins
- Prefill coalescing tweak: small change to coalescing window cut one extra prefill call in 60% of runs. Priya to land patch behind a feature flag by EOD 2026-11-11. Expected unit cost delta: -1.8%.
- Kernel threshold tuning: lower small-seq threshold from 32 -> 24 for one micro-kernel to see if we can reduce kernel switch overhead. Marcus to A/B this on internal perf cluster.

Action items (owner / due / success criteria)
- Marcus: Add allocator fallback to PR #1145 and re-run p4d-8s stress tests. Due 2026-11-12. Success: memory regression <=2% and preserved p99 improvement >=1.5x on small-seq bench.
- Priya: Prototype per-route eviction config API + console mock. Due 2026-11-19. Success: demo + API spec in Confluence.
- Daniel: Launch 48h canary for B2 on 5% traffic starting 2026-11-12. Due: launch 2026-11-12; report 2026-11-14. Success: meet rollback criteria or confirm safe.
- Aisha: Kernel-version tagging in traces + dashboard panel. Due 2026-11-15. Success: panel visible in Console showing comparative percentiles.
- Jenny K: Capture OOM repro artifacts 2026-11-11 02:00 PST and upload to linked ticket. Due 2026-11-11. Success: heap dump and allocations captured.

Risks / notes
- If kernel memory leak persists, we must freeze rollout for all hosted regions until a patch is validated. That impacts new Dedicated customers wanting to pin this kernel for lower p99.
- Mixing eviction policies in a single pool adds complexity to autoscaler decisions (hot partitions). Platform-eng should weigh in before per-route flags are made widely available.

Follow-ups / next sync
- Quick sync scheduled: 2026-11-12 09:30 PT (15m) to confirm canary kickoff and OOM repro collection.
- Full weekly runtime sync: 2026-11-17 10:00 PT.

Notes-to-self / raw thoughts
- Consider an automated rollout policy: only enable kernel patch in pools with >60% small-seq traffic. Could reduce blast radius.
- Maybe instrument token-level affinity to automatically pick eviction profile per session rather than per-route — heavier engineering but better UX.

Attachments & useful links
- Perf bench artifacts: https://s3.redwood-inference/internal/bench/v1145/2026-11-09/logs.tar.gz
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve-runtime/pull/1145
- Eviction study docs: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRV/kv-eviction-studies
- Jira: JIRA-RT-8721 (kernel mem regression)

End of notes.

Document history: created 2026-11-10 by Sofia Patel, updated 2026-11-11 with additional action item clarifications and new canary timing.
